lessons.title: Decision-making process and fundamentals of decision-making approaches.
lessons.description: This lesson provides an overview of how people make decisions, exploring the factors that influence good or bad choices and the main cognitive biases. It also discusses practical strategies for making decisions more quickly and efficiently. Finally, it delves into the understanding of outcome bias, showing the risks of evaluating decisions solely based on their outcomes.

lessons.title: Problem framing
lessons.description: This class combines theoretical references on decision-making frameworks and the balance between data and intuition with a practical group exercise. Students analyze the strategic dilemma of a rapidly growing Brazilian startup and must decide between international expansion, investment in new technology, or local consolidation. The dynamic challenges the groups to justify their choice, identify critical information, and reflect on when to rely on objective evidence or managerial instincts.

lessons.title: Decision-Making Tools I
lessons.description: In this instruction students will be presented with tools for decision-making, such as priority matrix, maximax, maximin, minimum regret.

lessons.title: Decision-Making Tools II
lessons.description: Introduces the Laplace Criterion (principle of insufficient reason) and the Hurwicz Criterion (weighted optimism/pessimism). This session teaches students how to find a middle ground in strategic planning when data is scarce.

lessons.title: Decision-Making Tools III
lessons.professor: Marcelo de Paula do Desterro Gorini
lessons.description: In this instruction, as a sequence of decision-making tools, students will learn the specifics on Decision Trees.

lessons.title: Heuristics and Biases
lessons.description: The lesson focuses on heuristics and cognitive biases in decision-making, exploring how these mental shortcuts influence choices in daily life and the professional environment. The aim is to understand that, while useful for simplifying decisions in uncertain contexts, heuristics can generate distortions, misperceptions, and systematic errors. At the same time, analyzing biases allows for the recognition of thought patterns that affect diverse areas such as business, health, and finance, offering insights to improve the quality of individual and organizational decisions.

lessons.title: Decision-Making Tools IV (Monte Carlo)
lessons.professor: Marcelo de Paula do Desterro Gorini
lessons.description: In this instruction, students will discuss how to make decisions supported by Monte Carlo tool.

lessons.title: Group decision-making process
lessons.professor: Marcelo de Paula do Desterro Gorini
lessons.description: This lesson addresses techniques and strategies for group decision-making, exploring practical ways to improve the collective process. Tools are presented to help groups organize ideas, evaluate alternatives, and reach more consistent consensus. Strategies for reducing common problems, such as conformity, excessive hierarchical influence, or reliance on a few opinions, are also discussed. The focus is on showing how structured behaviors and methods can make group decision-making more effective and balanced.

lessons.title: Decision Making in Companies
lessons.professor: Marcelo de Paula do Desterro Gorini

lessons.title: Decision-Making Tools V (Real Options)
lessons.professor: Marcelo de Paula do Desterro Gorini
lessons.description: In this instruction, students will be presented to an introduction of real option pricing.

lessons.title: Excel Data Modeling and Analysis for Business
lessons.professor: Marcelo de Paula do Desterro Gorini
lessons.description: This instruction presents concepts and practices of data modeling and analysis applied to business problems. Students use Excel to organize, process, and interpret information in a structured way. The focus is on transforming data into insights that support decision-making.

lessons.title: From Model Outputs to Business Recommendations
lessons.professor: Marcelo de Paula do Desterro Gorini
lessons.description: In this session, students learn how to translate the outputs of their Monte Carlo simulator into actionable business recommendations that a partner can understand and act upon. The lesson addresses one of the hardest transitions in data-driven decision-making, moving from a distribution of possible outcomes to a single defensible course of action. Students will examine the "flaw of averages" and why point estimates mislead executives, explore the six requirements of Decision Quality (appropriate frame, creative alternatives, relevant and reliable information, clear values and trade-offs, sound reasoning, and commitment to action), and practice articulating recommendations that explicitly acknowledge uncertainty, trade-offs, and confidence intervals.

lessons.title: Defending Decisions Under Uncertainty: handling questions and stakeholder pushback
lessons.description: This session prepares students for the final delivery banca, where they will defend their simulator and business recommendations to the partner and to the evaluation panel. The class focuses on the specific challenge of defending a decision that was made under uncertainty, where the analyst must simultaneously acknowledge the limits of the model and preserve the credibility of the recommendation. Students will study the four villains of decision-making (narrow framing, confirmation bias, short-term emotion, overconfidence) from Chip and Dan Heath's WRAP framework, with particular attention to "Attain Distance Before Deciding" and "Prepare to Be Wrong", both directly applicable to how one responds to stakeholder questions. The class also addresses the dynamics of advice-giving and advice-receiving, how to handle pushback from more powerful stakeholders, and how to reposition a recommendation without abandoning its core logic.

lessons.title: Decision-Making in the Age of AI
lessons.professor: Marcelo de Paula do Desterro Gorini
lessons.description: Artificial intelligence is reshaping how decisions are made but it has not replaced the need for human judgment. This lesson explores the evolving relationship between AI-powered tools and the decision-maker, examining when to trust algorithms, when to override them, and how to build decision processes that leverage the best of both.

lessons.title: Decision under Uncertainty
lessons.professor: Marcelo de Paula do Desterro Gorini

workbook_metadata.title: PESTEL Analysis
workbook_metadata.description: A PESTEL analysis is a strategic framework commonly used to evaluate the business environment in which a firm operates. Traditionally, the framework was referred to as a PEST analysis, which was an acronym for Political, Economic, Social, and Technological; in more recent history, the framework was extended to include Environmental and Legal factors as well.

workbook_metadata.title: “Data and Intuition: Good Decisions Need Both”
workbook_metadata.description: It explores the balance between decisions based on quantitative data and those that rely on intuition/experience, considering when each approach is most useful, and how to combine the two.

workbook_metadata.title: Problem Framing
workbook_metadata.description: What is problem framing, really? Problem framing is the process of discovering, analyzing, and defining the real strategic problem before committing to solutions. It connects your business objectives, customer needs, and constraints into a shared understanding of what is worth solving and why.

workbook_metadata.title: Are You Solving the Right Problem?
workbook_metadata.description: What does it take to build thought leadership that actually works in the market? This material explores problem framing, innovation inside real organizations, and why the best ideas start with solving a clear, meaningful problem. It also looks at how thought leadership grows beyond the book, turning strong concepts into practical tools, market relevance, and long-term business value.

workbook_metadata.title: Use of information sources by startup managers
workbook_metadata.description: This research focused on the use of information sources about the organizational environment by startup managers. It sought to characterize the relevance of sectors within the external environment to the business, the factors that motivate managers to seek information, and the degree of relevance and reliability of the information sources. The research methodology was based on a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods. For quantitative data collection, an online questionnaire was used, obtaining 60 responses. After analyzing the results, as a qualitative research method, interviews were conducted with three managers involved in incubation, acceleration, and investment programs for startups, so that the data could be discussed. The results demonstrated that entrepreneurs recognize customers and technology as the main sectors of the external environment affecting their businesses, and that there is a concern in seeking information to generate innovations and support decisions. Furthermore, it was possible to verify the relevance and reliability attributed to internal information sources, such as partners/employees and databases from their own companies, and the relevance of new digital information sources, to the detriment of traditional sources.

workbook_metadata.title: A systematic review of risky-choice framing effects
workbook_metadata.description: Classic decision theory requires that rational agents show description invariance: which description is chosen should not matter for judgments, preferences, or choices given the descriptions are co-extensive. Framing research has amply demonstrated a failure of description invariance by showing that the choice of the description has a systematic effect on judgments, preferences, and choices. Specifically, framing research has shown that linguistically different descriptions of seemingly equivalent options frequently lead to preference reversals.

workbook_metadata.title: DECISION MAKING IN UNCERTAINTY AND RISKY ENVIRONMENT
workbook_metadata.description: This article analyzes the processes and criteria for decision-making in environments of risk and uncertainty, using a practical case study of a business affected by the Covid-19 pandemic to illustrate the application of different decision-making theories and methods.

workbook_metadata.title: Decision Analysis 1b: Equally Likely (Laplace) and Realism (Hurwicz)

workbook_metadata.title: DECISION MAKING IN UNCERTAINTY AND RISKY ENVIRONMENT
workbook_metadata.description: This paper explores the theoretical and practical elements of decision-making under conditions of certainty, risk, and uncertainty, applying various analytical criteria to a real-world case study of a business navigating Covid-19 pandemic restrictions

workbook_metadata.description: This video tutorial demonstrates how to construct and solve a basic decision tree using the expected value approach to evaluate and choose the best investment alternative

workbook_metadata.title: How to analyze decision situations using Decision Tree
workbook_metadata.description: This video explains how to use decision trees to visually analyze multi-stage decision problems and calculate expected monetary values to determine the optimal course of action

workbook_metadata.title: Decision Making Under Uncertainty
workbook_metadata.description: This chapter provides a formal, quantitative framework for decision-making under uncertainty, demonstrating how tools such as expected monetary value, decision trees, Bayes' rule, and utility functions can be used to systematically evaluate alternatives, manage risk, and optimize business strategies

workbook_metadata.title: Using a Decision Tree to help Make Decision
workbook_metadata.description: This article explains how to use a decision tree, a visual flowchart tool that helps individuals navigate complex choices by mapping out possible options, probabilities, and outcomes to calculate and compare their overall expected values

workbook_metadata.title: Heuristics and Biases in Decision Making, explained
workbook_metadata.description: We all use heuristics to make everyday decisions — but sometimes they blind us to the truth. Therefore, we need to do something that isn't easy: accept that our ideas might be wrong.

workbook_metadata.title: The Impact of Cognitive Biases on Professionals' Decision‑Making
workbook_metadata.description: This study reviews how heuristics/biases affect professional decisions in different areas: management, medicine, finance, law. It shows which biases appear, how they interfere, their limitations, etc.

workbook_metadata.title: Heuristics and Biases in Judicial Decisions
workbook_metadata.description: The text uses the metaphor of three baseball umpires to discuss the illusion of impartiality in judgments. While one recognizes his human limitations, the others assume infallibility. From this, the article shows that judges, like any person, are also subject to heuristics and cognitive biases, which function as mental shortcuts to save resources, but can generate systematic errors in decisions. These biases influence everything from the analysis of evidence to sentencing, revealing that, despite experience and training, irrelevant factors can predictably distort judgments, casting doubt on the idea of total objectivity in the judicial process.

workbook_metadata.title: Video 1: How to Forecast with Confidence Using Monte Carlo Simulation | The Statistical CFO
workbook_metadata.description: The video demonstrates how CFOs and finance professionals can utilize Monte Carlo simulation to transition from instinct-based estimating to data-driven probability distributions, enabling them to confidently forecast financial outcomes and clearly communicate risks to stakeholders

workbook_metadata.title: Video 2: Monte Carlo Simulation Explained. Why Single Forecasts Mislead Decision Makers
workbook_metadata.description: This video explains why relying on single-number forecasts can be dangerously misleading, and introduces the Monte Carlo simulation as a powerful tool that explores thousands of possible futures to help decision-makers better understand and manage risk and uncertainty

workbook_metadata.title: Monte Carlo Simulation Made Super Easy!
workbook_metadata.description: This video provides a step-by-step guide on how to perform a 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation in Excel for a basic income statement, utilizing randomized functions and data tables to determine expected profit and calculate the probability of a financial loss

workbook_metadata.title: Business Question 3

workbook_metadata.title: Group Decision Making Techniques
workbook_metadata.description: The video demonstrates practical techniques that groups can use to improve their decision-making.

workbook_metadata.title: The Seven Pitfalls of Data-Driven Decision-Making (And How to Avoid Them)
workbook_metadata.description: The promised powers of incorporating data into decision-making read like an advertisement: Make decisions better, faster, and more accurately! Minimize uncertainty and maximize returns! Gain agility and accountability! Facilitate innovation and disruption in all the right ways! And in reality all the hype is as advertised—when data is done right. But when data is mishandled, ignored, or even tortured, it no longer delivers the same superlative benefits.

workbook_metadata.title: Making better decisions in groups
workbook_metadata.description: This text reviews the literature to identify common problems in individual and group decision-making. Using a Bayesian framework, it explains how past experiences and new evidence interact in exploring hypotheses about different world states and possible actions. It acknowledges that biases, often unconscious, make information processing more efficient, but do not always lead to the best decision. It highlights that group decisions can help overcome these biases and broaden the search for solutions, especially when there is diversity of members. However, diverse groups also face their own challenges, requiring appropriate management strategies to improve the quality of collective decisions.

workbook_metadata.title: Decision making in the age of urgency
workbook_metadata.description: Decision making takes up a lot of time, much of it used ineffectively. New survey results offer lessons for making quick, high-quality decisions that support outperformance.

workbook_metadata.title: When Analysis Outruns Wisdom: Potential Pitfalls of Data-Driven Decision-Making
workbook_metadata.description: This article discusses potential pitfalls that can arise from data-driven decision making when not properly balanced with human judgment, strategic thinking, and organizational context. Drawing on the author's experience as a management consultant, key risks are examined such as the "tyranny of metrics" when KPIs distort goals, misinterpreting correlations as causation, overgeneralizing from limited data sets, confirmation bias within "filter bubbles," and overemphasizing quantitative data at the expense of human elements. Specific industry examples are provided to illustrate unintended consequences that have occurred. The article advocates for maintaining a multidisciplinary, questioning approach to analytics, constantly reevaluating metrics and models, supplementing internal data with external realities, and blending quantitative and qualitative inputs. Balancing these risks and enacting various safeguards can maximize the benefits of fact-based management while avoiding potential downsides.

workbook_metadata.title: Exploring top management team intuition in strategic decision-making
workbook_metadata.description: Intuition plays an essential role in strategic decision-making, helping executives navigate complex and dynamic environments. This study surveyed managers from 27 UK companies about successful and unsuccessful intuitive decisions, identifying factors that enhance or diminish the effectiveness of intuition. The results offer theoretical and practical insights into how to use intuition more effectively in the decision-making process.

workbook_metadata.title: Video 1: The Essence of Real Option
workbook_metadata.description: This video explains how real option pricing can augment traditional discounted cash flow valuation by factoring in the value of learning and adaptive behavior, provided that the business decision meets the strict criteria of having an embedded option, possessing exclusivity, and satisfying the basic principles required to use these pricing model

workbook_metadata.title: The real power of real options
workbook_metadata.description: By applying financial options theory to strategic business investments, managers can better evaluate opportunities and proactively create value by leveraging flexibility and embracing uncertainty, which overcomes the limitations of traditional net-present-value analysis

workbook_metadata.title: Data Model in Excel - What is it? What is it used for?

With this tool, you can efficiently load and organize your data, allowing you to create customized queries for analysis and decision-making. In this video, we'll explore what the Data Model in Excel is and what it's used for—a tool that facilitates the organization and analysis of information for Business Intelligence professionals.

workbook_metadata.description: Article published in 2023 that applies Monte Carlo simulation and sensitivity analysis to real investment-decision cases in two companies. The authors walk through the full pipeline from stochastic modeling to tornado graph, spider chart, and profit sensitivity analysis, showing how each output informs a specific part of the business recommendation. Students should focus on how the authors present results to decision-makers and on how the sensitivity analysis is used to justify the final recommendation. Direct methodological reference for the Sensitivity Analysis Report artifact.

workbook_metadata.title: Risk Taking: A Corporate Governance Perspective
workbook_metadata.description: This paper examines how organizations make decisions under uncertainty and highlights the role of governance in managing risk-taking. It presents a structured framework for decision-making that integrates tools such as scenario analysis, decision trees, and probabilistic simulations to evaluate potential outcomes and downside risks.The key takeaway is that high-quality decisions are not defined by outcomes alone, but by the robustness of the process—particularly the explicit consideration of multiple scenarios, assumptions, and risk exposures. By formalizing this process, organizations enhance transparency, improve accountability, and strengthen the defensibility of executive decisions before boards and stakeholders.
workbook_metadata.parent_class: Defending Decisions Under Uncertainty: handling questions and stakeholder pushback

workbook_metadata.title: Strategic Intelligence: An Integrated Approach to Enterprise Risk Management
workbook_metadata.description: This article explores how organizations can enhance decision-making by integrating strategic intelligence into enterprise risk management (ERM). It emphasizes the importance of moving beyond traditional, compliance-driven risk frameworks toward a more forward-looking approach that incorporates scenario planning, stress testing, and continuous monitoring of external signals.The core idea is that organizations should actively test strategic assumptions under different scenarios, enabling leaders to anticipate potential disruptions and respond proactively. By doing so, management teams can make more resilient decisions under uncertainty, while boards gain greater visibility into key risks, underlying assumptions, and preparedness for adverse outcomes.Ultimately, the integration of strategic intelligence into ERM strengthens governance, improves the quality of strategic discussions at the board level, and supports more informed, transparent, and defensible executive decision-making.
workbook_metadata.parent_class: Defending Decisions Under Uncertainty: handling questions and stakeholder pushback
